To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ag+ induces two different types of contraction in frog skeletal muscle fiber.

Ag+ induced a phasic and subsequent tonic contractures in single fibers from the frog toe skeletal muscle, the phasic contracture was induced only in fibers with the intact T-tubule and the tonic contracture was induced in fibers with or without the intact T-tube, and the phasic contractures were not affected by TTX or DAP but the tonic contractures were affected by DAP and Ca2+.
the mechanism of Ag+ induced contractures in frog toe skeletal muscle fibers depends on the extracellular Ca2+ concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of extracellular Ca2+ concentration on the maximum amplitude of Ag+-induced contractures.
the mechanism of Ag+ induced contracture.
the effects of extracellular calcium concentration and Ca2+-channel blocker on the Ag+-inducible contractures in frog muscle fibers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the phasic contracture is due to a Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum via a voltage-sensitive Ca2+ channel on the T-tube membrane, whereas the tonic contracture is due mainly to a Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release.

the phasic contracture induced by Ag+ is not mediated by Na+, K+, or Ca2+ channels, but by some unknown mechanism which is independent of the T-tubules, whereas the tonic contracture is mediated by Ca2+ entering the fiber through the surface membrane and is inhibited by diltiazem.

the phasic contracture was due to Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum by Ag+ entering the T-tubules, whereas the tonic contracture was due mainly to the Ca2+ influx from the external space through the sarcolemma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ag+ induces two types of muscle contractures.
Ag+ induced a Ca2+ release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) via the T-tubule membrane, resulting in the phasic contracture.

Ag+ induced a phasic contracture in the fibers with intact T-system, whereas it induced a tonic one in the fibers with disrupted T-tubules, and the former was not affected by the external Ca2+ or the Ca2+ channel blockers, while the latter was dependent on both the external Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ag+-induction of contractures in frog muscle is a complex phenomenon.
the mechanism of Ag+-induced contractures is complex and involves both surface and T-tubular Ca2+ channels.
the phasic contracture induced by Ag+ is due to the influx of Ca2+ through the surface membrane, and the subsequent tonic contracture is due to the release of Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
